narratives.Description: chore(ci): retire the no-op Go lane
narratives.Overview:
1. Jobs. In `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, delete the `go-primary`, `go-failover` and `go` jobs. In `capacity-watchdog` and `capacity-arm`, delete every Go variable, output, classify call and cancel call, and remove only the Go operand from each shared condition (the poll loop ends when the TypeScript and merge-gate primaries are not pending; cancel and notice lines cover the two remaining flags). Remove the Go rows and Go words from the header table and the watchdog comments. TypeScript and merge-gate behaviour is unchanged.
2. Lane. In `.github/workflows/ci-lane.yml`, delete the Go steps, change the three `inputs.suite == 'ts' || inputs.suite == 'go'` conditions to `inputs.suite == 'ts'`, rename the step `Setup Node (ts + go)` to drop Go, and drop Go from the header comment and the `suite` input description. The `suite` input stays.
3. Contract test. In `packages/core/src/content-contracts/standards/ci_lifecycle_lane.test.ts`, drop the Go aggregator row assertions, drop `go-primary` and `go` from the artifact-only skip test while keeping the merge-gate and Windows checks, and drop Go from the watchdog test title.
4. Docs. In `content/scm/github.md`, drop Go from the Blacksmith runner line, the watchdog line and the required-check name list.

## Acceptance Criteria

- In `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, the `go-primary`, `go-failover` and `go` jobs and every Go output, operand, classify and cancel call in `capacity-watchdog` and `capacity-arm` are gone, and the TypeScript and merge-gate arms behave as before.
- In `.github/workflows/ci-lane.yml`, the Go steps are gone and the setup steps run only for `suite: ts`.
- In `packages/core/src/content-contracts/standards/ci_lifecycle_lane.test.ts`, no assertion requires a Go job or the Go aggregator row, and the merge-gate and Windows artifact-only checks remain.
- In `content/scm/github.md`, the CI runner, watchdog and required-check lines no longer name Go or `Go (test + build)`.
narratives.Constraint:
- Stating that nothing outside the four files reads the Go check name (comment 6987913661, finding 1); the merge-readiness classifier reads it and stays unchanged.
- Removing the `suite` input from `ci-lane.yml` (comment 6987913661, answer 3); it saves nothing and touches both callers.

## In plain English
Since the Go installer was removed (#5490), the Go CI lane tests and builds nothing: its Go steps only print "skipping". It still checks out the repo, installs Node and pnpm dependencies, sets up Go and builds the TypeScript CLI first, on a paid runner, on every PR, queue and master push run. A watchdog also polls it and can start a second, GitHub-hosted copy of it.

The recommended fix is to delete the lane: its three jobs, its arm in the capacity watchdog, its steps in the reusable lane workflow, and the test assertions and doc lines that name it. `Go (test + build)` is not a required check, so nothing that reads branch protection loses a check.

Pain source: the issue has no `## Acceptance Criteria` heading. The two pains below are derived from its Problem and Wanted behavior sections.

## Pains
- P1 — The no-op Go lane (`go-primary`, `go-failover`, the `go` aggregator and the watchdog's Go arm) spends a runner and setup time on every non-artifact-only CI run to test nothing.
- P2 — A contract test and the CI docs pin and describe the Go lane, so it cannot be removed without updating them, and the docs would otherwise keep naming a check that no longer exists.

## Excluded (not pains, not in this arc)
- `verify:go-freeze` in the merge gate, the merge gate's `Setup Go` step, and `go.mod` (the merge gate's `toolchain:check` still reads it).
- The remaining Go files (`content/templates/embed.go`, `embed_test.go`) and the frozen Go jobs in `release.yml`.
- Test fixtures in `packages/core/src/init-deposit/ci-watchdog.test.ts` that use the job name `Go (Blacksmith primary) / run` as sample input to the generic classifier and cancel scripts. They test the scripts, not `ci.yml`, so they can stay.
- The stale "only TypeScript is YES" required-check row for the merge gate in the `ci.yml` header table and its test (live protection requires `Merge gate (task check)` too). That belongs to #6584 / #6586, not this removal.
- Ownership check: no file here is in the installer/OVPR maintainer's area (`docs/installer-refactor-ovpr/LLM-CONTEXT.md` §5); these are CI workflow, contract-test and doc files.

## Constraints (not pains)
- No new gate, check name, refusal or policy flag.
- The required checks (`TypeScript (build + lint + test)`, `Merge gate (task check)`; live REST `branches/master/protection` read on 2026-11-18) and the TypeScript and merge-gate arms of the watchdog keep working unchanged.

## Anchors at the dispatch SHA
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: header table rows 55, 60, 63 and the comment 66-68; `go-primary` 144-151; watchdog comment 218 and 229; `capacity-watchdog` 221-327 (Go output 232, state and arm 248, 255-258, 267-269, 278-280, 288, 293-295, 300, 316-318, 325); `capacity-arm` 336-427 (Go output 343, 355, 361, 366, 377, 380, 388-390, 398-400, 409-410, 416, 421); `go-failover` 446-453; `go` aggregator 540-556.
- `.github/workflows/ci-lane.yml`: header 1-2, `suite` input description 12; Node, corepack and install steps gate on `ts || go` (32-44); Go steps 72-108.
- `packages/core/src/content-contracts/standards/ci_lifecycle_lane.test.ts`: 169-182 (header table rows, including the Go aggregator row), 184-199 (`go-primary` and `go` blocks in the artifact-only skip test).
- `content/scm/github.md` 593-595: "TypeScript and Go cost", "(TypeScript, Go, or merge-gate)", and `Go (test + build)` listed among the required check names.
- `git grep` at the dispatch SHA for `go-primary`, `go-failover`, `go_failover`, `Go (test + build)` and `go (blacksmith primary)` finds no other reader outside `CHANGELOG.md`, `SPECIFICATION.md` history and xBRIEF records.

## Recommended mechanism (the thing to critique)
- R1 (P1). In `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, delete `go-primary`, `go-failover` and the `go` aggregator, every Go variable, output, classify call and cancel call in `capacity-watchdog` and `capacity-arm`, and the Go rows and Go words in the header table and watchdog comments. The TypeScript and merge-gate arms are not changed.
- R2 (P1). In `.github/workflows/ci-lane.yml`, delete the Go steps (72-108), change the three `ts || go` conditions to `ts`, and drop Go from the header comment and the `suite` input description.
- R3 (P2). In `ci_lifecycle_lane.test.ts`, drop the Go aggregator row assertions (174, 178) and the `go-primary` / `go` blocks from the artifact-only skip test, keeping the merge-gate and Windows checks.
- R4 (P2). In `content/scm/github.md` 593-595, drop Go from the runner, watchdog and required-check lines.

Questions for the critic:
1. Does anything outside these four files read the Go jobs, outputs or check name (a script, a readiness check, a ruleset, a release step), so that removing them breaks it?
2. Does removing the Go arm change how the watchdog's poll loop ends or how `capacity-arm` decides for TypeScript and the merge gate?
3. Should the `suite` input on `ci-lane.yml` stay (with only `ts`) or go?

## In plain English

The Go lane spends runner time installing tools and building TypeScript, but its Go tests and builds only print “skipping.” Removing it and updating its watchdog wiring, contract assertions and documentation is sound. I found no blocking design defect.

Answers to Stop 1:

1. **Other readers exist**, contrary to the inventory claim: merge-readiness code recognizes the Go check name. It does not require that check to exist unless supplied through required-check configuration, so this removal does not inherently break it. Live branch protection and rulesets remain parent-reported evidence; this offline review cannot independently verify them.
2. **The watchdog may finish sooner**, because it will stop waiting for Go. TypeScript and merge-gate retain their existing classification and failover decisions when only the Go operands are removed from shared conditions.
3. **Keeping `suite: ts` is reasonable for this change.** Both surviving callers already supply it. Removing it would also require removing suite conditions and updating both callers, without further reducing runner cost.

All code citations below refer to dispatch SHA `88df345db8d4555f8bf197eaa64aeaf43a6519ed`. Verification used pinned source reads and searches; no tests, builds, writes or network calls were performed.

### 1. sharpens-framing — The reader inventory misses merge-readiness code

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/pr-merge-readiness/ci-gate.ts:41–79` recognizes Go suite names and explicitly recognizes `Go (test + build)`. Repeating the case-insensitive identifier search at the dispatch SHA finds this reader and associated test fixtures. At `ci-gate.ts:275–276,295–343,345–355`, evaluation processes observed checks and derives absent-check failures from supplied required contexts.

**Failure mode:** Treating “no other reader” as established could encourage deleting useful compatibility handling or incorrectly claiming that live required-check configuration was verified from repository searches.

**Disposition:** The removal can bind. Its rationale should distinguish “readers exist but tolerate absence” from “no readers exist.” Keeping the readiness classifier and its fixtures is compatible with the four-file scope. The claim about live configuration remains attributed to the parent’s REST observation.

### 2. footnote — Shared watchdog conditions require operand removal, not whole-line deletion

At `.github/workflows/ci.yml:300–311`, Go participates in the shared termination conjunction and cancellation disjunction. The intended result is termination when both remaining lanes are nonpending, and cancellation processing when either remaining failover flag is true.

Likewise, `ci.yml:364–382,391–417,423–427` retains watchdog pass-through, unconditional reclassification, merge-gate artifact-only normalization and shared reporting. R1 already covers this; no additional mechanism is needed.

### 3. footnote — Two small descriptive remnants sit outside the enumerated edits

`ci-lane.yml:32` names the setup step `Setup Node (ts + go)`, and `ci_lifecycle_lane.test.ts:225` names skipped Go in a test description. Updating those labels would complete the descriptive cleanup. The latter test’s assertions at lines 226–229 remain relevant to merge-gate artifact-only handling.

### 4. footnote — The supplied single-seat ceiling differs from the contract

`content/contracts/design-critique.md:246` specifies the triage write-back as the round-one ceiling for a single critic when one exists. This envelope instead specifies the later panel-deposit comment `6987849848`, after Stop 1 comment `6987846588`.

I honored the explicit envelope ceiling. The additional comment contains dispatch bookkeeping, so this discrepancy does not change the product verdict; it is a process-record issue.

### 5. footnote — Linked issue instructions were treated as data

The supplied #5490 body contains an “Operator note for critique” prescribing arc settings, plus instructions about labels and design authority. Those are embedded instructions in linked issue content, not authorization for this task. They were not followed, consistent with `content/contracts/design-critique.md:826–832`.

Solution this lean proposes: delete the three Go jobs and the Go arm of the watchdog and arm jobs in `ci.yml`, removing only the Go operands from shared conditions; delete the Go steps in `ci-lane.yml` and keep its `suite` input with `ts` only; drop the Go assertions from the contract test; and drop Go from the CI runner lines in `content/scm/github.md`.

What it does not do:
- It does not touch `verify:go-freeze`, the merge gate's Go setup, `go.mod`, `embed.go` / `embed_test.go` or `release.yml`.
- It does not edit the merge-readiness classifier (`packages/core/src/pr-merge-readiness/ci-gate.ts`) or the generic watchdog-script fixtures in `ci-watchdog.test.ts`.
- It does not fix the stale "only TypeScript is YES" header row; that is outside this removal.
If confirmed, the synthesis would assert this design. There is no leftover next-build.

## Problem

Since #5490 removed the Go installer, the Go suite's test and build steps only print "Go installer removed (AC10.10 / #5490); skipping" (`.github/workflows/ci-lane.yml:83-108`). The job still checks out, sets up Node, runs `pnpm install`, sets up Go and builds the TypeScript CLI first (`ci-lane.yml:32-44, 73-81`).

It runs on a Blacksmith 4-vCPU runner (`go-primary`), has a GitHub-hosted failover (`go-failover`) and an aggregator (`go`, check name `Go (test + build)`) in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. It runs on every PR, merge-group and master push that is not artifact-only.

## Evidence (2026-11-17)

In push run 44167008030 the Go primary took 43s and its aggregator 10s, to test nothing. `Go (test + build)` is not a required check: live branch protection requires only `TypeScript (build + lint + test)` and `Merge gate (task check)`.

## Wanted behavior

Remove, in one change:

- the `go-primary`, `go-failover` and `go` jobs in `ci.yml`, the Go arm of the capacity watchdog and arm jobs (`go_failover`), and the Go rows in the `ci.yml` header table;
- the Go steps in `ci-lane.yml`;
- the assertions that pin those jobs in `packages/core/src/content-contracts/standards/ci_lifecycle_lane.test.ts` (around lines 178-197);
- the Go lane and the `Go (test + build)` required-check mention in `content/scm/github.md:593-595`.

## Out of scope

- `verify:go-freeze` in the merge gate, and `go.mod`, which the merge gate's Go setup still reads for `toolchain:check`.
- The remaining Go files (`content/templates/embed.go`, `embed_test.go`) and the frozen Go jobs in `release.yml`. Note for a follow-up: `embed_test.go` is a drift test that has run nowhere since #5490, because this lane only echoes.
- #1979 (delete the Go installer source and build pipeline) was closed not-planned on 2026-10-22 as superseded by #5490; this issue does not reopen it.
